title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཚེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 187)
shelf_note: Canonical Tibetan Buddhist philosophical commentary on Pramana (logic and epistemology) from the Derge Tengyur collection.

tr_errors_B.english: then the question "is one of them eating?" or "is it one or the other?" would be meaningless.
tr_errors_B.problem: Misinterprets the classical Sanskrit logical example involving 'kill one of the two' (ekataraṁ māraya / gcig cig sod dam) and invents 'would be meaningless'

tr_errors_B.english: because this is an instance of considering the consciousness accompanied by a plurality.
tr_errors_B.problem: Mistranslates the verbal participle sems pa (considering / reflecting, parallel to bsam pa) as the noun 'consciousness'

pages.prefer_reason: Translation A is faithful to the Pramāṇa terminology and accurately renders the classical logical debate formulas, whereas Translation B garbles the stock example of 'killing one' (sod).

book_verdict: Clear woodblock print of the Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa section with completely accurate OCR; Translation A is precise and faithful to the epistemological text.
